description_good: README.md describes what the website does (app directory, one-command installers, signed downloads, blog, docs, shared accounts), with an English summary: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/README.md
interact: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue forms explain how to obtain the source, report bugs, request features and contribute: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the pull request process: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: Conventional Commits, tests with every behaviour change, all CI checks green (format, lint with zero warnings, typecheck, tests, CodeQL, gitleaks, npm audit): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi: Apache-2.0 is OSI approved; GitHub detects the license as Apache-2.0.
license_location: The license is in the standard location LICENSE at the repository root: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics: docs/README.md is the documentation index (architecture, development, testing, deployment, auth, release signing): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/docs/README.md
documentation_interface: The external interfaces are documented: canonical URLs in docs/url-convention.md, auth and roles in docs/auth.md, the signed-release API and JWKS in docs/release-signing.md: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/docs/release-signing.md
sites_https: The project website https://tsudev.com, the repository and downloads all use HTTPS only (HSTS max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload).
discussion: GitHub Issues and pull requests are public, searchable, URL-addressable and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/issues
english: README.md has an English summary, CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md are in English, and the issue forms accept reports in English or Vietnamese: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
maintained: Actively maintained: dozens of merged pull requests in the last month: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
repo_public: Public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev
repo_track: git records who changed what and when; every change goes through a pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/commits/main
repo_interim: Every change, including work in progress, is pushed to branches and merged into main through pull requests in the public repository: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/pulls?q=is%3Apr
repo_distributed: git (a distributed version control system) on GitHub.
version_unique: tsudev.com is deployed continuously. Every production deployment of main gets a unique calendar version tag deploy-YYYY.MM.DD.N (vYYYY.MM.DD.N before 17 Nov 2026), created automatically after the deploy by scripts/release-tag.js: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/tags
version_semver: Versions use Calendar Versioning (CalVer) YYYY.MM.DD with a micro counter .N for several deployments on the same day, e.g. deploy-2026.11.17.7. The deploy- prefix keeps website deployments apart from app release tags (vYY.M.DDNN) across the tsudev ecosystem.
version_tags: Each deployment is an annotated git tag on the deployed main commit: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/tags (script: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/scripts/release-tag.js)
release_notes: Each version has human-readable release notes: the annotated tag message lists every merged pull request since the previous version (shown at https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/releases), and CHANGELOG.md summarises each tagged deployment: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns: No vulnerability with a CVE or similar public identifier has been fixed in this project. Such fixes would be named in the tag release notes and published as a GitHub Security Advisory (SECURITY.md).
report_process: Bug reports go to GitHub Issues using the bug report form: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/issues/new/choose
report_tracker: GitHub Issues with bug report and feature request forms: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/issues
report_responses: No external bug report has been filed so far (the repository became public on 21/08/2026); the maintainer reads every issue and would acknowledge reports within days.
enhancement_responses: No external enhancement request has been filed so far; the feature request form routes them to the maintainer, who answers each one.
report_archive: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md describes how to report vulnerabilities (English section included): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to a reply within 7 days.
build: npm workspaces: npm ci, npm run build:ts (services, compiled with tsc) and the OpenNext build for Cloudflare Workers; the backend Docker image is built and booted in CI: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/actions/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools: Standard tools: npm, the TypeScript compiler, Next.js/OpenNext, Docker, cargo for the small Rust/WASM signing component.
build_floss_tools: Node.js, npm, TypeScript, Next.js, OpenNext, Prisma, Docker and Rust are all FLOSS.
test: About 90 unit/integration test files (Jest) in services/*/test, apps/frontend-main/test and packages/*/test, Rust tests for the signing component, and Playwright end-to-end tests in e2e/tests: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/tree/main/services/auth-service/test
test_invocation: Standard invocation per workspace: npm --workspace <workspace> test (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/testing.md): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/docs/testing.md
test_most: Tests cover authentication (passwords, 2FA, passkeys, sessions, OIDC), authorization, release sealing and Ed25519 signing, storage presigning, the public pages (ISR fallback, CSP, XSS boundary with property-based tests) and end-to-end smoke tests of the main pages.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions runs unit tests against a real PostgreSQL, the Rust tests, the backend Docker boot test and Playwright E2E on every pull request and push to main; these checks are required by branch protection: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'A change in behaviour comes with a test in the same pull request ... A bug fix comes with a regression test that fails without the fix': https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Recent changes add tests with the code, e.g. #265 (OIDC sign-in and account security, 17 test files), #258 (Turnstile), #266 (React #418 on ISR pages), #261 and #260 (install script gate tests): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added: The test requirement is written in CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template asks how the change was tested: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
warnings: TypeScript strict mode (tsconfig.base.json), ESLint with typescript-eslint and react-hooks rules, Prettier, plus a second type-check with TypeScript 7 in CI: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/tsconfig.base.json
warnings_fixed: ESLint runs with --max-warnings 0 and type errors fail the build, so warnings are fixed before merge (package.json lint script): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/package.json
warnings_strict: TypeScript strict is on for every workspace and the lint gate allows zero warnings.
know_secure_design: The maintainer documented the assets, threat model and defence layers (server-side decisions, fail-closed role checks, least privilege, defence in depth): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/docs/security-plan.md
know_common_errors: docs/security-plan.md and docs/auth.md cover the common web errors and their mitigations: XSS (CSP with hashes, sanitized Markdown with property tests), injection (Prisma parameterised queries), credential stuffing (rate limits, breached-password check), session fixation/revocation, header spoofing of client IPs: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/docs/auth.md
crypto_published: Only published algorithms: Argon2id, SHA-256, HMAC, AES-256-GCM, scrypt, Ed25519, ECDSA P-256 (ES256), WebAuthn.
crypto_call: No primitives are implemented in the project: it calls Node.js crypto, @node-rs/argon2, the WebAuthn library and the Rust ed25519-dalek crate (compiled to WASM): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/packages/trust-crypto/Cargo.toml
crypto_floss: All cryptographic libraries (Node.js/OpenSSL, @node-rs/argon2, ed25519-dalek, jose/WebAuthn libraries) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength: Ed25519 and ECDSA P-256 (128-bit security), AES-256-GCM, SHA-256; TLS is terminated by Cloudflare with modern key lengths.
crypto_working: No broken algorithms are used for security. SHA-1 appears only in two standard-mandated places described under crypto_weaknesses.
crypto_weaknesses: No default security mechanism depends on a weakened algorithm. Two SHA-1 uses are mandated by standards and do not rely on collision resistance: HMAC-SHA1 in TOTP (RFC 6238, required by authenticator apps) and the 5-character SHA-1 prefix of the Have I Been Pwned k-anonymity range API used only to detect breached passwords: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/services/auth-service/src/password.ts
crypto_pfs: HTTPS is terminated by Cloudflare with TLS 1.3/1.2 ECDHE key exchange only (TLS 1.0/1.1 refused), which provides perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage: User passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes with per-password salts (19 MiB memory, 2 iterations, OWASP parameters) via @node-rs/argon2; only auth-service reads the hash: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/services/auth-service/src/password.ts
crypto_random: Keys, tokens, salts, IVs and one-time codes use Node.js crypto.randomBytes/randomInt (CSPRNG); Math.random is not used for security: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/services/auth-service/src/tokens.ts
delivery_mitm: The website and every download are served over HTTPS only with HSTS preload; downloaded release files are additionally verifiable with server-computed SHA-256 and Ed25519 signatures (public keys at /.well-known JWKS).
delivery_unsigned: Hashes and signatures are never retrieved over plain HTTP; release SHA-256 and signatures are served over HTTPS and computed by the server, never supplied by the uploader (docs/release-signing.md).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: No unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity: 0 open Dependabot and code scanning alerts, npm audit --omit=dev must show 0 High/Critical in CI. The only known advisory is GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 (deepmerge, LOW, development-only via Jest, no fixed version yet).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability is open; security issues found in the project (e.g. client IP spoofing for rate limits, 05/11/2026) were fixed within a day.
no_leaked_credentials: No valid credentials in the repository: gitleaks scans the full history on every push and pull request, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, and production secrets live only in Render/Cloudflare: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/actions/workflows/security-scan.yml
static_analysis: CodeQL on every push and pull request plus weekly, OpenSSF Scorecard, ESLint and TypeScript strict: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL JavaScript/TypeScript security queries look for XSS, injection, path traversal, SSRF, insecure randomness and similar vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed: 0 open code scanning alerts; findings (e.g. CodeQL #99 TOCTOU) are fixed or dismissed with a written reason.
static_analysis_often: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis: Property-based testing with fast-check (thousands of random inputs) of the Markdown XSS boundary runs in CI, plus Playwright end-to-end tests against the running site: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsudev/blob/main/apps/frontend-main/test/md.property.test.ts
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: No C/C++ or other memory-unsafe language is shipped. The code is TypeScript plus a small Rust signing component compiled to WebAssembly; its few unsafe FFI entry points run inside the bounds-checked WASM sandbox and are covered by Rust tests in CI.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: Tests run with Jest/Playwright assertions and TypeScript runtime checks; the property tests assert the security invariants on every generated input.
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No exploitable medium or higher vulnerability has been found by dynamic analysis; findings are fixed and turned into regression tests.
